text:
priya: Noticed psionic13b-int4 canary hitting intermittent OOMs on dedicated nodes. Mostly during long sessions (>800 tokens) after ~2h uptime. Logs show repeated 'alloc fail' from tiling allocator and high slab fragmentation. Anyone recognise this pattern with memory_tiling + aggressive prefetch?
kevin: Yep. Aggressive prefetch + int4 KV layout can cause slab churn. What are the canary defaults currently?
priya: Canary model config: `max_new_tokens=1024`, `batching.max_concurrent=8`, `prefetch_window=64`, `memory_tiling.enabled=true`, `memory_tiling.prefetch_bias=0.9`. Repro rate ~6% on 1:1 traffic.
maya: 0.9 prefetch_bias is high for int4. It will hoard many KV slots, causing fragmentation under tight slab allocs. Recommend drop to 0.5 and reduce concurrency during rollout: `batching.max_concurrent=2`.
sam: Also enable soft evict and a kv_trim_threshold around 0.6 so we reclaim slots gracefully. Suggest: `memory_tiling.prefetch_bias=0.5`, `memory_tiling.soft_evict=true`, `memory_tiling.kv_trim_threshold=0.6`.
kevin: For safety set `max_new_tokens=256` for this variant and enforce `client_max=1024` at route level. Turn on per-request `kv_eviction="on-epoch"` to avoid unbounded growth in long-lived requests.
priya: Rolling a small patch to two canary hosts: prefetch_bias=0.5, max_new_tokens=256, batching.max_concurrent=2. Will monitor metrics.
infra-bot: deploy 6181912345 by priya to eng-dedicated-canary at 2024-11-05T15:40:12Z — success
sam: Quick smoke earlier: with bias=0.9 int4 P50 similar but P95 +200ms and lots of slab churn. With bias=0.5 P95 down ~120ms and fragmentation traces look calmer.
maya: Before wider rollout run a short quality eval: long-form summarization set (100 samples) compare int4 vs int8. If Rouge/L delta >1.5% we hold.
priya: Good call. Starting 24h canary + eval job. If OOMs stop and quality delta <1% we'll roll to 10% traffic.
kevin: Small operational tweak: add slot_reserve=0.08 to allocation policy to keep headroom for hot allocations. Saved us in past incidents.
priya: Added slot_reserve 0.08. Will post metric snapshots in ~2h. :thumbsup:
